hypothesis: Sparse short-flank counts may poorly estimate local rate; wider flanks can reduce count noise but may introduce spatial heterogeneity.
site_support: all archived label-free training coordinates, unchanged
rate_disagreement: absolute log2((left_count+0.5)/left_exposure) minus log2((right_count+0.5)/right_exposure); report median and 90th percentile; 0.5 is explicit prior support
bias_model: unchanged frozen five-seed mitochondrial parametric ensemble
diagnostic: per-strand central background count, zero-count frequency, finite-sequence coverage and left/right exposure-adjusted rate disagreement for every task and window
limitations: More finite expectations do not establish better footprints.
Wider windows may cross accessibility boundaries or include regulatory signal.
A later accuracy comparison requires a separate execution freeze.
No uncertainty, safety or runtime claim transfers from earlier operators.
